summary: Foundations for auto-resume after a usage limit, for every chat, behind the staged flag limit_auto_resume (LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED in src/shared/limit-resume.ts, false; SB_LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME=1 or the backend setting labs.limit_auto_resume turns it on). This change adds the limit_resumes table (one row per root conversation: instance, limited turn, reset time, state, request id, streak, disarm reason), its CRUD, the setting chats.autoResumeAfterLimit (on by default, no UI yet), and the pure rules limitState, shouldArm, fireChecks, nextStreak and the resume turn wrapper, with shared fixtures. Nothing reads the flag outside tests, so no behaviour changes. The migration time is logged through the db.migrate perf span. Limit classification: the Claude and Codex adapters put an optional limit { limitClass, resetAt } on the end event of a turn that ended on a usage limit or a full context window (no limit means other), the registry logs one 'turn limit' counter line per such turn, and the synthetic model name the Claude CLI writes on its limit messages is never recorded or shown as the model. Nothing reads the limit field yet, so no chat behaves differently. Desktop runner (this change, still behind the flag): src/main/provider/limit-resume.ts arms the chat's row on the end event of a usage-limited turn with a reset time, keeps one timer per armed row at the reset plus a minute (rebuilt at startup), and at fire time checks again (still armed with the same request id, not archived, no open card, same account, a fresh usage reading says the window is open). It then sends the wrapped resume turn through the approval result turn path and releases the held queue behind it, stores a [[sb:limit-resume]] row and publishes limit-resume.changed. A resumed turn that fails or hits the limit again within 5 minutes counts in the streak; the third gives up. Stop (interrupt), archive, Cancel auto-resume and a normal turn end before the reset disarm the row durably. Channels provider:limit-resume-enabled, -get, -cancel and -resume-now; the desktop Limited row (LimitResumeRow: Resumes HH:MM, Resume now, Cancel auto-resume) and the Settings, Accounts switch Resume after a usage limit resets show only while the flag is on. Every fire logs a limit-resume.fire perf span with its outcome, and arms, give-ups and resumed-turn outcomes log one info line each, so resume success can be counted. Phones and push (this change, still behind the flag): the backend advertises capability limit_auto_resume_v1 (the provider:limit-resume-* channels and limit-resume.changed exist; with the flag off, get answers none, so no row shows). The Expo thread screen shows the same Limited row as the desktop (LimitResumeRow: Resumes HH:MM, Resume now, Cancel auto-resume, or why no resume is armed), read on open and on every limit-resume.changed; an older backend without the capability keeps the held message's Resume only. limit-resume.changed carries gaveUp on the one change that gave up, and the push notifier sends 'Auto-resume gave up after 3 tries. Resume by hand.' for it. The give-up count is the existing 'limit resume outcome' line with gaveUp true; the Limited row reads go through the generic slow IPC span.

The Expo Limited row (OTA lane, JS only) shows only against a backend with limit_auto_resume_v1 and the flag on; the stored [[sb:limit-resume]] row shows as a notice through systemRowView.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: The release that turns limit_auto_resume on by default (LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED true), after the Android Limited row ships (PR 4b) and beta users run it for a week. The Android app reads turn.completed by field, so the optional limit field is ignored until then. SyntheticUserMessage.kt drops the resume turn's block (fixture case limit-resume-turn); the stored resume row shows as Switchboard notice and limit-resume.changed is ignored until the Android Limited row ships. The Android app ignores the limit_auto_resume_v1 capability and the gaveUp field until its Limited row ships (PR 4b); the 'Auto-resume gave up' push reaches it as an ordinary error push.

The labs switch reaches beta users first. This change touches no package identity, signing, deep link or native module, and its migration is additive, so an older build opens a migrated database.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resume-rules.test.ts tests/unit/hub-db.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: limitState, shouldArm, fireChecks and nextStreak pass every case in tests/fixtures/limit-resume-cases.json; the flag helper is off by default and on with SB_LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME=1 or labs.limit_auto_resume; limit_resumes arms, fires once per request id, disarms durably, keeps the streak and keys a rotated Claude id by its root conversation.
A copy of a real 1.1 GB desktop database migrated with this build (five new tables, no other change), and the migrate code of origin/main then opened the migrated file.

npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-classification.test.ts tests/unit/acp-generic-adapter.test.ts tests/unit/codex-protocol-schema.test.ts: every case of tests/fixtures/limit-classification-cases.json passes through the real Claude adapter (SDK messages), the real Codex adapter (app-server notifications, then a failed turn/completed) and the generic ACP adapter for Gemini (a fake agent whose prompt fails with a quota error, which stays other). A full context window is context_full, not a limit; a limit followed by an empty success stays a limit; the synthetic model is never recorded and adds no tokens. The Codex fields read (error.codexErrorInfo, turn.error.codexErrorInfo) are in the app-server schema fixture.

tests/unit/limit-classification.test.ts also checks that a Claude rejection while no turn runs carries no limit, and that a late Codex limit error of a stopped turn does not mark the running turn. Full suite: npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2, 7062 passed, 4 skipped; npm run typecheck green.

npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resumer.test.ts tests/unit/provider-registry-limit-resume.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 (fake clock, real migrated database): a chat limited with a reset in 2 minutes resumes by itself a minute after the reset; Stop before the reset means no resume, also after a restart; an armed row's timer is rebuilt at startup; 3 quick failures give up; a resumed turn that ends normally resets the streak; Resume now with the window still closed keeps the row armed; a closed window at the reset re-arms to the new reset; setting off or flag off arms nothing; no reset time asks for a manual resume; a full context window is not a limit; a normal turn end before the reset disarms; one limited turn that ends twice arms once; an open card or a chat that is not running delays the fire; another account disarms; a failed send arms again; a fire that finds a turn running tries again later; a Stop between a limit and its late second end keeps the row disarmed; a new limit starts its streak at 0. In the registry, with the limited turn and a queued message both counted as outstanding, Resume now sends the resume turn as a turn of its own (not queued) before the held queue resumes, and stores and publishes the resume row.
Full gate: npm run typecheck green; npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2, 7126 passed, 4 skipped.

notExercised: No live usage limit was hit on Claude, Codex or an ACP agent: the runner was checked with a fake adapter and a fake clock, and the classification cases are captured or constructed frames.
A chat whose session is not running at the reset (after a restart, or a closed chat) resumes only when its session starts again; restart recovery is a later change.
A message you send while the chat is idle and limited runs at once (today's behaviour) instead of joining the held queue; a message queued behind the limited turn does run after the resume turn.
The Expo Limited row was not run on an iPhone or against a live limit; it is checked by the jest component test and the mobile typecheck. The Android Limited row comes in a later change (PR 4b).
